title: A direct summand of a projective module is projective
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $M$ a projective $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] and $P$ an $R$-module. (1) If there are $R$-linear maps $i:P\to M$ and $s:M\to P$ with $s\circ i=\mathrm{id}_P$, then $P$ is projective. (2) In particular, if $P\cong M$ as $R$-modules, then $P$ is projective.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 05CF (lemma-characterize-projective, line 18795), proof of (2) => (1): $\mathrm{Hom}_R(P\oplus Q,-)=\mathrm{Hom}_R(P,-)\times\mathrm{Hom}_R(Q,-)$, so a direct summand of a module whose Hom functor is exact has an exact Hom functor.
